text:
oliver: Seeing a bunch of ML batch jobs stuck Pending in eu-west2. Events say 'Insufficient gpu'. Anyone else?
priya: Yeah saw that earlier. Pattern is large-pod requests (4x A100 style) can't fit even though free GPUs exist across nodes.
sasha: sounds like fragmentation. We have lots of nodes with 1-2 free GPUs scattered. Scheduler won't pack across nodes for single-pod requests.
matt: Can you paste `kubectl describe pod` / scheduler events?
oliver: Paste of event: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  5m    default-scheduler  0/24 nodes are available: 24 Insufficient gpu, 6 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
```
priya: Also noticed many nodes have `node.kubernetes.io/priority=low` taint from spot/interruptible pools. That reduces candidates.
infra-bot: autoscaler: scale-up recommended for group gpu-eu-west2-large by 2 nodes (requested by controller). :gear:
matt: autoscaler kicked but ASG capped at 10 for that pool; we hit cap. We should either increase cap or allow burst to shared pool.
sasha: short-term: could we allow binpacking via `TopologySpreadConstraint` tweaks or scheduleHint? But the scheduler won't merge across nodes. Better to consolidate small allocations.
priya: Proposed rollout: 1) enable descheduler job nightly to consolidate single-GPU pods onto fewer nodes; 2) allow preemptible pool fallback for 4-GPU pods (tolerations addition); 3) bump ASG cap by 2 while we defrag.
matt: Agree. Also consider adding a packed node class: `gpu-packed` (bigger instance types) and route large pods there via nodeSelector + PodAffinity to prefer co-located GPUs.
oliver: Quick test: I ran `kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU_FREE:.metadata.annotations/gpu-free` and got mixture. Output snip: 
```
node-123   1
node-124   0
node-125   2
node-126   0
node-127   1
node-128   3
```
priya: node-128 has 3 free GPUs but we need 4 for the pod, so scheduler can't place it. That's the fragmentation.
sasha: Can we change the allocator plugin to support `best-effort` packing? Dangerous for latency-critical jobs but could help batch training.
matt: Not without testing. Alternative: implement a short-lived defrag job that cordons small-free nodes, drains single-gpu tenants into fewer nodes (evict low-priority pods), then uncordon. Schedule during off-peak.
priya: Eviction policy: only evict pods with QoS BestEffort or low priorityclass, and keep preemptionBudget. We'll add a 10% headroom so we don't thrash.
oliver: Who wants to own the defrag script + runbook? I'll draft the script if someone reviews.
sasha: I'll review and add safety checks. Also add a metric to alert when >10 pending large-pod scheduling attempts in 5m.
matt: I'll open infra ticket to increase ASG cap temporarily and track cost delta.
infra-bot: ticket #INFRA-4283 created: 'eu-west2 defrag + temp asg bump' assigned to matt.
priya: One more note: network bandwidth on older instances is a constraint for consolidating high-throughput training. We must mark nodes with `net-high=true` label for real packing targets.
oliver: Good call. For the immediate fix: matt + oliver will bump ASG cap and run defrag script in a maintenance window tonight. pr iya and sasha will prepare tests and alerts.
sasha: :thumbsup: keep me posted in the morning if any regressions.
matt: Will post ASG change + cost estimate after bump.
oliver: Thanks — will post results here after the run.
